A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PoisonedFL research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments across five datasets, including attack comparisons, ablations, tailored defenses, and synthetic-data experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and reports additional trajectories of sign alignment and accumulated model-update magnitude.

M1.justification: The fixed random sign vector, adaptive magnitude construction, hypothesis-test-based scaling, and adaptive attacks remain unchanged. Equations 1–11 are retained across the main text and appendices.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MNIST, FashionMNIST, Purchase, CIFAR-10, and FEMNIST with the same classification tasks. The synthetic-data experiments and tailored-defense scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: The main attack and defense comparison sets are unchanged. However, v2 Table 5 reports Opt. Fang in the Purchase/Multi-Krum update-norm comparison, whereas v3 Figure 8a omits its series despite retaining its name in the shared legend.

E3.justification: The reported dataset splits, architectures, training settings, participation rates, attack parameters, and defense procedures remain unchanged. The new trajectory plots disclose intermediate results without establishing a change to the underlying experimental protocol.

E4.justification: v3 Figures 7–8 extend the mechanism diagnostics from the summaries in v2 Tables 4–5 to trajectories across training rounds. This adds evidence about how alignment and attack magnitude accumulate; the existing sensitivity studies, ablations, and countermeasure analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same six-seed sign-vector experiment and the same across-round means and standard deviations for filtering and trust-score diagnostics. No additional uncertainty-estimation or repeated-run practice is reported.

E6.justification: All 405 numerical entries in Table 1 are unchanged. v3 adds intermediate diagnostic results and replaces exact summaries with trajectories: for example, v2 Table 5 gives a Median update norm of 7.09×10², while v3 Figure 8b reaches approximately 3.9×10² at round 6000. Identical endpoint conditions are not established, so this is not evidence of a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: v3 removes the explicit global FL objective minimizing the sum of client losses from Section 2.1. This is a limited removal of formal background; the attack optimization problems, mathematical update rules, and binomial hypothesis-testing argument remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central claims about multi-round consistency, minimal attacker knowledge, defeating eight defenses, and outperforming seven attacks. The tailored-defense contribution remains in the introduction and appendices despite its omission from the revised abstract.

C2.justification: The explanations of attack accumulation, defense failures, adaptive evasion, and normalization limitations retain their meaning. The cross-silo applicability limitation is preserved in Appendix D.3; relocation and wording refinements do not establish a new substantive interpretation.

D1.justification: v3 adds a source-code access statement and repository link in the abstract. Most implementation information is retained, although the explicit FLTrust trust-score normalization formula and its accompanying explanation from v2 Appendix A.1 are omitted.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Byzantine-robust decentralized federated learning, Do We Really Need to Design New Byzantine-Robust Aggregation Rules?, and FedREDefense. It removes AFLGuard, the client-side distribution-inference study, and FedRecover. The broad research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 substantially shortens the introduction and background and reorganizes the narrative. Motivation, dataset descriptions, ablations, countermeasures, synthetic-data discussion, and detailed limitations are redistributed into supplementary Sections A–D.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column layout to a two-column format, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. Two diagnostic tables become trajectory figures, and the filtering table’s incorrect False Positive Rate row label is corrected to False Negative Rate.

improvement.justification: v3 provides more informative temporal evidence for the accumulation mechanism, adds a code-access pointer, and corrects the filtering-rate label. These are limited gains because the main empirical findings remain unchanged. Replacing exact diagnostic tables with plots reduces numerical accessibility, and the omitted Opt. Fang series weakens one supplementary comparison, but the overall revision modestly improves the paper’s usefulness.
